linux.note: theme_color colors a GTK header bar on the Linux app, with black or white title text, when it is written as #rgb or #rrggbb. The header bar then replaces the window manager's title bar. ios.note: theme_color fills the area behind the iOS status bar and picks dark or light status bar text by contrast, when it is written as #rgb or #rrggbb. macos.how: LSMinimumSystemVersion and the swiftc target (13.0 unless set; 15.2 with a Kotlin web service; 15.4 with a Java web service, whose TeaVM WebAssembly also needs exception references, ADR 0083, or a Dart web service, whose loader imports the JavaScript exception tag WebAssembly.JSTag, ADR 0033); a value below that floor stops the build (TY1601). Component styles need Safari 17.4 or newer for CSS @scope, and the build notes it (ADR 0108). Dart and Java page services built at 15.4 and a Kotlin one at 15.2 answered a click in the macOS app on macOS 27.2, and a component style stayed inside its component there (MA7)

windows.note: On Windows, tac.application.minimumSystem.windows is the WebView2 Runtime version (118.0 unless set, the first with CSS @scope for component styles; 119.0 with a Dart or Kotlin web service, which WebView2 119 runs with the JavaScript exception tag Dart imports; 137.0 with a Java web service, whose TeaVM WebAssembly also needs exception references; ADR 0108, ADR 0083). The app checks it when it starts and explains a missing or older runtime instead of opening a blank window.

linux.note: On Linux, tac.application.minimumSystem.linux is the WebKitGTK version (2.40 unless set; 2.46 with a Kotlin web service; 2.48 with a Java web service, whose TeaVM WebAssembly also needs exception references, ADR 0083, or a Dart web service, whose loader imports the JavaScript exception tag WebAssembly.JSTag, ADR 0033). The app checks it when it starts and explains an older WebKitGTK instead of opening a blank window. Component styles need WebKitGTK 2.44 or newer for CSS @scope, the first release that ran it in GP1; WebKitGTK comes with the distribution, so the floor stays 2.40 and the build notes it (ADR 0108).

ios.how: MinimumOSVersion and the swiftc target (17.4 unless set, the first with CSS @scope for component styles; 18.2 with a Kotlin web service; 18.4 with a Java web service, whose TeaVM WebAssembly also needs exception references, or a Dart web service, whose loader imports the JavaScript exception tag WebAssembly.JSTag; ADR 0108, ADR 0083, ADR 0033); a value below that floor stops the build (TY1601). On the iOS 17.4 and 18.2 simulator runtimes (MA5) the main gate passed and Go and linked Rust services kept their component style inside the component; a Kotlin app at 18.2 answered on 18.2 and was refused at install on 17.4, a Java app at 18.4 was refused on 18.2, and a Dart app found no WebAssembly.JSTag on 18.2, which moved Dart to 18.4. Java and Dart page programs built at 18.4 ran on the iOS 26.5 simulator (MA8)

android.note: On Android, tac.application.minimumSystem.android is the minSdk API level (26 to 35). Dart web services need Android System WebView 119 (WebAssembly garbage collection and the JavaScript exception tag), Java web services need WebView 137 (exception references, ADR 0083), and component styles need WebView 118 for CSS @scope; Google Play updates the web view apart from Android, so neither need raises the API level (ADR 0108). The host bridge needs a System WebView with WEB_MESSAGE_LISTENER; the app checks for it at startup and shows a refusal page naming the installed WebView instead of loading a page without native calls. scripts/android/web-view-refusal-test.mjs saw the refusal on an Android 8.0 (API 26) emulator with WebView 58.0.3029.125, and the app opened normally on an API 35 emulator with WebView 124 (GP2). A Java page service and a Java page program ran on an Android 17 (API 37) emulator with WebView 145 (MA9).

web.how: every route already has its own address; with hosts listed, the web build writes /.well-known/apple-app-site-association when TAC_APPLE_TEAM_ID is set and /.well-known/assetlinks.json when tac.origin and TAC_ANDROID_CERT_SHA256 are set, and /.well-known/windows-app-web-link when TAC_WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE_PUBLISHER is set, and prints a note for each one it cannot write

macos.note: tac.application.links: the macOS app claims the listed schemes in Info.plist and opens their links at their route, or at start_url when the route is unknown. A signed --release build whose TAC_MACOS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE has the Associated Domains capability embeds the profile and claims the listed hosts with applinks: entries, and the app opens their universal links at their route; other builds leave links to the hosts in the browser. No signed build has opened a link from a hosted domain yet.

windows.note: tac.application.links: the Windows app registers the listed schemes for the current user when it starts (a --release MSIX package declares them as windows.protocol extensions instead), and opens their links at their route, or at start_url when the route is unknown. A link that arrives while the app runs goes to the open window. A --release MSIX package also declares the listed hosts as app URI handlers, and the web build writes /.well-known/windows-app-web-link when TAC_WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE_PUBLISHER is set; Windows then opens links to the hosts that the shell launches in the app, while links clicked in Edge or another browser stay in it. The unpackaged app, and a package registered from a folder in Developer Mode, leave links to the hosts in the browser. An installed signed package opened a shell-launched link from a hosted domain at its route (LINKS).

linux.note: tac.application.links: the Linux .desktop file claims the listed schemes once it is installed, as the release .deb and AppImage do, and the app opens their links at their route, or at start_url when the route is unknown. A link that arrives while the app runs goes to the open window. Linux has no verified web links, so links to the listed hosts stay in the browser.

ios.note: tac.application.links: the iOS app claims the listed schemes in Info.plist and opens their links at their route, or at start_url when the route is unknown. With TAC_APPLE_TEAM_ID set, the app claims the listed hosts with applinks: entries and opens their universal links at their route: a simulator build opened links from a hosted domain on a cold start and while running (LINKS). A --device or --release build needs a profile with the Associated Domains capability; no signed build has opened one on a device yet.

android.note: tac.application.links: the Android app claims the listed schemes, and https links to the listed hosts with autoVerify, and opens them at their route, or at start_url when the route is unknown. Android verifies the hosts only when each one serves /.well-known/assetlinks.json with the app's signing certificate (TAC_ANDROID_CERT_SHA256); until then it asks which app opens their links. On the emulator, a verified hosted domain opened its links in the app without asking (LINKS); a physical device has not been checked.

windows.note: tac.application.window.titleBar "integrated" lets the Windows page reach the top edge under the system caption buttons, with the same insets as macOS and drag regions that WebView2 handles (ADR 0098). The menu bar moves into the window menu (Alt+Space, or a right-click on a drag region). The page covers the top edge, so the window resizes from its sides and bottom. On a signed-in Windows 11 desktop the page started at the top edge, the caption buttons kept their own hit testing, a drag in a drag region moved the window, a right-click opened the window menu and hovering maximize showed Snap Layouts (SD1).

web.how: same-origin requests to the Yon server

macos.note: The macOS app's pages load from tachyon-app://bundle, so same-origin requests reach no Yon. Pages and linked Swift and Rust HTTP clients reach the Yon at tac.yon.origin, run on macOS by scripts/native/yon-reach-test.mjs (NET1, LR1). The page holds a linked Rust service's stream and socket clients, and that run reached Yon through them too (LR1). The page holds a linked Swift service's stream and socket clients and delivers their messages to it (LS1); TAC_YON_SERVICES=swift yon-reach-test.mjs ran that on macOS (MA1). WebAssembly Kotlin and C# services reach it through HTTPClient in the macOS app too (scripts/native/wasm-features-app-test.mjs, MA7).

windows.how: the app's pages load from https://tachyon.local, so Yon calls go to tac.yon.origin across origins, from the page and from linked Rust and C# services; the page holds linked C# (NET3, LS1) and Rust (SW1) services' stream and socket clients, and a linked Rust service hears a topic (SW1), in scripts/windows/yon-reach.ps1 on a signed-in Windows desktop. WebAssembly Swift and Kotlin services reach it through HTTPClient, hold its stream and socket clients, and answer through a Setup http adapter in the Windows app too (scripts/native/wasm-features-app-test.mjs, SW4); other absolute URLs go only to the hosts in tac.outgoing.hosts

linux.note: The Linux app's pages load from tachyon://app, so same-origin requests reach no Yon. HTTP calls, streams, sockets and topics from pages and linked Rust services reach the Yon at tac.yon.origin, which lists tachyon://app in server.origins, run under Xvfb and on WSL by scripts/linux/yon-origin-native-test.mjs (NET4, RL1). WebAssembly Swift, Kotlin and C# services reach it through HTTPClient in the Linux app too (scripts/native/wasm-features-app-test.mjs, LX3).

ios.note: The iOS app's pages load from tachyon-app://bundle, so same-origin requests reach no Yon. Pages and linked Swift and Rust HTTP clients reach the Yon at tac.yon.origin, run on the iOS simulator over http and https by scripts/native/yon-reach-test.mjs (NET1, LR1). The page holds a linked Rust service's stream and socket clients, and that run reached Yon through them too (LR1). The page holds a linked Swift service's stream and socket clients and delivers their messages to it (LS1); TAC_YON_SERVICES=swift yon-reach-test.mjs ran that on the iOS simulator over http and https (MA1). WebAssembly Kotlin and C# services reach it through HTTPClient and hold its stream and socket clients in the iOS app too (scripts/native/wasm-features-app-test.mjs on the iOS 26.5 simulator, MA8).

android.note: The Android app's pages load from https://appassets.tachyon.local, so same-origin requests reach no Yon. HTTP calls, streams, sockets and topics from pages, and linked Kotlin and Rust HTTP clients, reach the Yon at tac.yon.origin, run on the Android 15 emulator by scripts/android/yon-origin-test.mjs and rust-services-test.mjs (NET2, MR2). The page also holds a linked Kotlin service's stream and socket clients and delivers their messages to it (LS1); TAC_YON_SERVICES=kotlin yon-reach-test.mjs ran that on the Android 15 emulator (MA2). The page holds a linked Rust service's stream and socket clients and delivers their messages to it too; TAC_YON_SERVICES=rust yon-reach-test.mjs ran that on the Android 15 emulator (MA9). WebAssembly Swift and C# services reach it through HTTPClient in the Android app (scripts/native/wasm-features-app-test.mjs, MA9).
